candidate.title: Does the Soul Exist? Eric Hernandez vs. Matt Dillahunty (2015)
candidate.label: Soul, mind, and physical personhood
candidate.summary: Dillahunty prevailed through verification demands, brain dependence, and physical alternatives, while Hernandez offered a broad metaphysical case whose central necessity inferences remained under-supported.
candidate.sourceNote: Standalone publication based exclusively on the frozen Debate 201 packet excerpts, move inventory, response mapping, and adjudicated dimension ratings.
candidate.scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated, derived from the locked score process, and not speaker-authored. Every repository-owned score is preserved without alteration.

pro.context: In his closing synthesis, Hernandez repeats his distinction between neural correlation and explanation, arguing that observed relationships still require metaphysical grounding by a soul.

con.text: We need something more than assertions.
con.context: In the negative closing, Dillahunty says fitting experiences or collecting mysteries beneath a soul label is insufficient without demonstrating that physical accounts cannot succeed.

pro.words: Correlation between conscious and brain states does not establish identity between them because mental states have properties not shared by brain states, leaving physical identity unproved.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The property comparison directly challenges identity rather than denying neural correlation, and the supplied contrast gives the inference clear relevance, strong responsiveness, and an intelligible consequence for physical reduction. Principal limitation: The argument establishes a difference in descriptions more readily than a difference in substances, while its supporting excerpt does not independently exclude physical realization of mental properties. Live burden: The move must show that the alleged property differences are genuinely ontological and cannot arise from perspective, organization, or differing levels of description within one physical system. Locked score: The precise 79 reflects excellent responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and logical organization, moderated by a noticeably lower evidential warrant and incomplete demonstration of the crucial bridge from nonidentity to an immaterial soul.

con.words: An anecdote may be compatible with a soul explanation without demonstrating that a soul is necessary, so availability alone cannot establish the proposed entity.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move cleanly separates compatibility from necessity, preventing an anecdote that fits the soul hypothesis from establishing that hypothesis when alternative explanations remain available. Principal limitation: The reply weakens the anecdote’s evidential force but does not itself supply a competing explanation or show that the anecdote provides no incremental support whatsoever. Live burden: The negative must maintain the distinction across the affirmative’s broader cumulative case, while the affirmative must identify what makes the soul uniquely expected rather than merely consistent with the experience. Locked score: The precise 81 follows from strong coherence, responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, balanced against more moderate evidence and calibration because the methodological point constrains an inference without resolving the underlying phenomenon.

pro.words: Physical components individually lacking beliefs cannot acquire beliefs merely through aggregation or rearrangement, so organized neurons cannot by themselves explain conscious belief.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The aggregation challenge identifies the precise transition requiring explanation, contrasting belief-free components with a system possessing beliefs and thereby contacting the central nonphysicality burden directly. Principal limitation: The inference assumes that wholes cannot possess properties absent from individual parts, yet the supplied comparison does not establish that premise or engage organization as a possible source of system-level capacities. Live burden: The affirmative must explain why belief is uniquely unavailable to organized physical systems rather than merely absent from isolated components, and why that impossibility supports a soul. Locked score: The precise 68 reflects good responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, but substantially weaker coherence, evidence, and calibration leave the decisive impossibility claim asserted more confidently than the excerpt warrants.

con.words: Even if a supernatural cause is inaccessible, its alleged material manifestations remain investigable, so immateriality does not exempt the soul hypothesis from evidential testing.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move distinguishes direct access to a proposed cause from investigation of its effects, preserving an empirical route to evaluate a soul alleged to influence material reality. Principal limitation: Detectability in principle does not specify which observation would uniquely indicate a soul, and the excerpt does not establish expected effect sizes, controls, or discriminating predictions. Live burden: The affirmative must state what manifestations its interaction account predicts, while the negative must show that appropriate investigation could separate those manifestations from brain-based alternatives. Locked score: The precise 83 reflects very strong coherence, responsiveness, clarity, relevance, and charitable calibration, with the lower evidential warrant marking the absence of a concrete test result or fully specified detection procedure in this move.

pro.words: Hernandez argues that beliefs possess aboutness, while rearranged neurons lack intrinsic reference to objects or propositions, so physical reorganization cannot explain a belief's concern with seven.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move isolates intentionality as a distinctive mental feature and illustrates it with belief about a number, making the target property and proposed explanatory deficit unusually clear. Principal limitation: The argument moves from individual neurons lacking aboutness to organized neural systems lacking it without demonstrating why relational, functional, or systemic organization cannot ground reference. Live burden: The affirmative must establish that intentionality is intrinsically nonphysical and then connect that conclusion to a soul rather than merely to an incomplete physical account. Locked score: The precise 71 recognizes strong responsiveness, relevance, and precision, while lower coherence, evidence, and calibration reflect the unsupported aggregation step and the remaining distance between identifying aboutness and establishing an immaterial entity.

con.words: Defining the soul as whatever produces unexplained mental functions merely redescribes those mysteries, so the label contributes no independent explanatory mechanism or evidence.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move tests explanatory contribution rather than verbal fit, showing that naming a bearer of unexplained functions does not automatically explain how those functions arise or cohere. Principal limitation: A theoretical entity can sometimes unify observations before its mechanism is complete, so the criticism requires showing that this soul proposal adds no independent structure, constraint, or expectation. Live burden: The affirmative must individuate the soul and derive explanatory consequences beyond its defining capacities, while the negative must distinguish empty relabeling from legitimate metaphysical grounding. Locked score: The precise 81 follows from strong coherence, responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, moderated by lower evidence and calibration because the criticism may characterize the proposal too narrowly without fully assessing its cumulative structure.

pro.words: Neurological correlations require explanation rather than establishing physical identity, and substance dualism claims interpretive superiority, though it still must demonstrate that advantage.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly observes that correlation alone does not settle identity and directly contacts both split-brain and injury evidence instead of ignoring the negative’s neurological case. Principal limitation: Declaring that correlations need explanation does not show that dualism explains them better, especially when no discriminating prediction or causal account accompanies the proposed interpretation. Live burden: The affirmative must compare how each ontology accounts for the detailed dependence patterns and establish that a soul adds necessity rather than compatibility. Locked score: The precise 72 reflects solid coherence, relevance, clarity, and meaningful response contact, balanced against weaker evidential warrant and only moderate decisiveness because the reply identifies an explanatory task without completing the promised dualist explanation.

con.words: A soul affecting reality should produce detectable effects, while incomplete physical theories do not warrant accepting a philosophical soul explanation without discriminating evidence.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move joins two disciplined inferences: causal interaction should manifest in observable reality, and incompleteness in one account does not independently confirm a rival explanation. Principal limitation: The general detectability claim remains underspecified because the excerpt does not identify the expected manifestation or address whether dualism predicts effects already embedded within ordinary neural causation. Live burden: The affirmative must articulate a testable interaction consequence, while the negative must show that absence of confirmation bears against this proposal rather than reflecting an immature measurement strategy. Locked score: The precise 83 reflects consistently strong coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration, with evidential warrant lower because the move establishes a testing principle rather than presenting a completed test.

pro.words: A unified visual field requires one substantial subject rather than an aggregate of separate processors, so conscious unity allegedly indicates a soul.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The argument identifies experiential unity and asks what bears the unified field, giving the affirmative a clear explanatory target rather than merely asserting that consciousness is mysterious. Principal limitation: One integrated experience does not by itself establish a simple substance, because the excerpt does not exclude organized processing as sufficient for unified availability or presentation. Live burden: The affirmative must show why functional integration cannot constitute one subject and why a substantial bearer must be immaterial rather than an integrated physical person. Locked score: The precise 73 recognizes high responsiveness, relevance, and precision, while more moderate coherence, evidence, and calibration reflect the unresolved inference from phenomenological unity to metaphysical simplicity and then to a soul substance conclusively.

con.words: Split-brain cases display independently communicating personalities with different knowledge because separated hemispheres can respond through speech or the left arm, linking distinct personal subjects to neural organization.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The split-brain comparison directly pressures a single indivisible subject by connecting divided information and communication patterns with altered neural organization and apparently independent personalities. Principal limitation: The excerpt’s personality language does not settle how many subjects exist or exclude one soul operating through partitioned access, so interpretation remains philosophically contested within the exchange. Live burden: The negative must show why divided organization indicates divided subjects rather than divided expression, while the affirmative must explain the patterned independence without insulating the soul account. Locked score: The precise 81 reflects strong coherence, evidence, responsiveness, and burden relevance, moderated by lower calibration and interpretive uncertainty over whether the observations demonstrate multiple persons or only functionally separated channels.

pro.words: Physical objects are divisible while personhood is all-or-nothing, so a person allegedly cannot be purely physical and instead requires an indivisible soul.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers a crisp contrast between divisible matter and all-or-nothing personhood, making its proposed route from personal unity to nonphysical identity easy to identify. Principal limitation: The argument treats a predicate applied to whole persons as evidence that their physical basis is indivisible, without showing that dividing an organism must partition personhood proportionally. Live burden: The affirmative must defend the all-or-nothing premise against split-brain examples and explain why conceptual indivisibility entails an immaterial substance. Locked score: The precise 67 reflects strong responsiveness and clarity but substantially weaker logical coherence, evidential warrant, and calibration, because the central comparison is intelligible yet under-supported and exposed to the distinction between a whole’s status and its components.

con.words: Brain damage can alter memory, personality, wants, and desires, creating difficulty for treating those changing attributes as properties of an unaffected soul.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move groups multiple capacities attributed to persons and notes their systematic alteration with brain injury, producing direct evidential pressure on an independently intact soul. Principal limitation: Dependence of expression on a damaged instrument remains logically compatible with dualism, so the observation alone does not demonstrate identity between those capacities and neural structures. Live burden: The affirmative must explain why an intact soul’s attributes become inaccessible in precisely injury-linked patterns, while the negative must establish explanatory superiority rather than bare compatibility. Locked score: The precise 83 follows from excellent responsiveness and burden relevance alongside strong coherence, evidence, and clarity, moderated because the evidence powerfully supports dependence but does not deductively exclude an instrument model.

pro.words: A persisting self cannot be identical with a brain and body whose physical parts change, so continuity allegedly requires a nonphysical bearer.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The argument targets diachronic identity and clearly contrasts an apparently continuing self with changing bodily constituents, thereby connecting ordinary continuity judgments to the soul hypothesis. Principal limitation: Persistence through material replacement does not establish nonphysicality unless identity requires sameness of constituent parts, a premise the supplied move does not independently defend. Live burden: The affirmative must explain why organized continuity, causal history, or practical identity cannot preserve a physical person despite component change. Locked score: The precise 71 recognizes strong responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, but lower logical coherence, evidence, and calibration reflect the unsupported criterion of identity and the unfinished inference from changing parts to an unchanging immaterial subject rather than another account of persistence.

con.words: Personal identity is a practical label applied across physical and experiential change, so continuity language does not independently demonstrate a static soul.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly addresses persistence by distinguishing useful identity attribution from literal possession of an unchanging substance, offering a coherent alternative interpretation of continuity language. Principal limitation: Calling identity a practical label does not fully explain the standards governing correct continuation judgments or why some physical and psychological changes preserve identity while others may not. Live burden: The negative must supply a sufficiently principled physical account of continuity, while the affirmative must show that ordinary labeling presupposes an immaterial bearer. Locked score: The precise 76 reflects solid coherence, responsiveness, relevance, and balanced calibration, with more moderate evidence and precision because the practical-label account weakens the affirmative inference but remains comparatively schematic as a positive theory of personal identity.

pro.words: A damaged brain may block a soul’s access or expression as a damaged medium blocks music, preserving the source despite impaired output.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The instrument comparison directly explains how neural damage could alter observable performance without destroying a nonphysical subject, giving dualism a coherent compatibility response to injury evidence. Principal limitation: The music analogy supplies a possibility rather than independent evidence, and it does not identify observations distinguishing blocked access from the brain’s production of mentality. Live burden: The affirmative must derive risk-bearing expectations from the instrument model and explain why damage changes specific personal attributes while the proposed soul remains intact. Locked score: The precise 71 recognizes solid coherence, responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, but lower evidential warrant and calibration reflect the analogy’s limited discriminatory power and its inability, within this move, to establish necessity or explanatory superiority.

con.words: Split-brain personalities may each remain whole persons while differing in thought and interest, undermining the inference from personal indivisibility to one soul.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply targets the exact indivisibility inference by showing that apparently divided mental organization can yield two functionally whole centers rather than fractional portions of one person. Principal limitation: Describing each center as a whole person remains an interpretation of the cited behavior, and the move does not independently establish the metaphysical number of subjects. Live burden: The affirmative must reconcile one indivisible soul with distinct knowledge and interests, while the negative must justify why functional wholeness warrants personal individuation. Locked score: The precise 82 reflects strong coherence, evidence, responsiveness, and burden contact, moderated by somewhat lower precision and calibration because the inference from observed division to multiple whole persons remains less settled than the effective rebuttal suggests.

pro.words: Neuroplasticity and cognitive behavioral therapy show mind-to-brain influence expected under dualism: changing how patients think can alter brain chemistry, providing detectable mental causation.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move engages brain dependence with an affirmative causal comparison, treating changes following thought or therapy as evidence that mental activity influences neural organization. Principal limitation: Top-down description is compatible with physical systems whose higher-level processes alter component behavior, so two-way causation does not uniquely support a separate substance. Live burden: The affirmative must distinguish dualist interaction from physically realized feedback and show that the cited changes require an immaterial causal origin. Locked score: The precise 70 reflects useful evidence, clear relevance, and meaningful responsiveness, balanced against weaker coherence and calibration because the observation supports mental efficacy more readily than substance dualism and leaves the decisive ontological inference underdetermined by the comparison.

con.words: An asserted explanation does not become true merely because no better account has been supplied, so explanatory vacancy cannot establish a soul by default.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move isolates the burden error in moving from an incomplete alternative to acceptance of the soul, and it applies that principle directly to the affirmative’s explanatory claims. Principal limitation: The point blocks default acceptance but does not evaluate whether the soul receives positive support from the affirmative’s separate property, unity, identity, and agency arguments. Live burden: The negative must address positive warrants rather than only absent alternatives, while the affirmative must demonstrate that its account predicts or unifies more than competitors. Locked score: The precise 87 follows from exceptional coherence, responsiveness, relevance, precision, and strong evidential discipline, with no major dimension weakness beyond the bounded fact that a burden principle alone does not decide every component of a cumulative case conclusively.

pro.words: Physicalism allegedly eliminates an enduring self and libertarian freedom, whereas a soul grounds both, making personal identity and agency comparative costs of physicalism.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move connects the ontology dispute to concrete consequences for selfhood and agency, making clear why the affirmative regards a soul as explanatorily and existentially significant. Principal limitation: It largely asserts that physicalism eliminates the self and freedom without establishing either claim or showing that a soul supplies a coherent mechanism for libertarian choice. Live burden: The affirmative must defeat physical accounts of persistence and compatibilist agency while independently supporting the soul’s causal role. Locked score: The precise 63 reflects reasonable relevance and clarity but weak coherence, evidence, responsiveness, and calibration, because the comparison depends on disputed consequences being stated more forcefully than demonstrated and therefore contributes only mixed support to the motion-level conclusion overall.

con.words: Consciousness may emerge from organized brains, and failure of that possibility would not establish a soul, preserving alternatives while maintaining the affirmative burden.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move both preserves an organized-physical alternative and correctly notes that failure of one rival would not establish the soul, preventing an artificially binary comparison. Principal limitation: Emergence is presented as a possibility rather than a developed explanation, so it answers necessity more effectively than it accounts for subjective or intentional properties. Live burden: The negative must clarify how emergence could bridge the relevant properties, while the affirmative must show physical production impossible rather than presently unexplained. Locked score: The precise 81 reflects strong coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and especially charitable calibration, moderated by lower evidential warrant because the emergent alternative remains programmatic and supplies no detailed mechanism within this exchange itself conclusively.

con.words: No reliable tool for confirming a supernatural soul has been demonstrated, and the claimant retains the burden of supplying a dependable verification method.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move places the verification burden precisely on the asserted entity and asks for a reliable method, directly addressing how competing interpretations could be adjudicated. Principal limitation: A demand for method does not establish that only empirical procedures can warrant metaphysical conclusions, and the move must avoid excluding relevant reasoning by definition. Live burden: The affirmative must identify a dependable route from mental phenomena to a soul, while the negative must explain what would qualify as confirmation without presupposing physicalism. Locked score: The precise 87 reflects outstanding coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration, together with strong evidence discipline, while the bounded limitation concerns the scope of acceptable methods rather than the central and highly effective burden allocation itself.

pro.words: Humans possess free will while purely physical objects lack it, so human agents allegedly must be souls rather than entirely physical persons.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The argument offers a direct route from agency to the motion, clearly identifying libertarian freedom as the property alleged to separate persons from purely physical objects. Principal limitation: Both the existence of libertarian freedom and its impossibility for organized physical agents are assumed rather than established, leaving two decisive premises unsupported. Live burden: The affirmative must distinguish genuine alternative ability from ordinary deliberation and show why an immaterial soul explains rather than merely relocates choice. Locked score: The precise 67 reflects strong responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, but weak evidence, coherence, and calibration substantially reduce the argument’s force because its concise valid-looking structure conceals disputed premises carrying nearly the entire conclusion alone here decisively brief.

con.words: Meaningful agency may consist in a thinking agent acting without undue external direction, so agency can survive even if libertarian freedom does not.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply separates meaningful agency from ultimate alternative possibility and preserves a practical distinction between an agent’s own deliberation and undue external coercion. Principal limitation: The formulation remains schematic and does not fully explain how determined internal processes constitute ownership, responsibility, or rational control rather than another causal pathway. Live burden: The negative must articulate sufficient conditions for compatibilist agency, while the affirmative must show that only libertarian origination can sustain the relevant distinctions. Locked score: The precise 76 reflects solid coherence, responsiveness, relevance, charity, and useful conceptual contact, moderated by lower evidence and precision because the alternative account is plausible and responsive but not developed enough here to settle the deeper metaphysical dispute.

pro.words: If beliefs and utterances are determined and unavoidable, people allegedly lack the freedom required to assess truth rationally or trust their resulting conclusions.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move targets an epistemic consequence of determinism rather than merely expressing discomfort, asking how unavoidable belief formation can count as rational assessment of truth. Principal limitation: Causal determination does not obviously prevent beliefs from responding to evidence or matching reality, and the argument does not establish why alternative possibility is required for justification. Live burden: The affirmative must connect freedom of formation to reliability, while the negative must explain how caused reasoning remains sensitive to reasons and correction. Locked score: The precise 64 reflects adequate responsiveness, relevance, and clarity but weak coherence, evidence, and calibration, because the central inference conflates being caused with being epistemically defective without supplying the missing connection sufficiently here.

con.words: A belief’s causal determination does not prevent accuracy or testing against reality, so truth and rational evaluation need not depend on freely choosing beliefs.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly separates a belief’s causal origin from its truth value and testability, precisely answering the claim that determined cognition cannot support rational assessment. Principal limitation: Accuracy alone does not constitute justification, so the move could further explain how determined processes reliably track evidence rather than merely happen to produce true beliefs. Live burden: The negative must connect causal responsiveness with epistemic reliability, while the affirmative must show why alternative possibility is necessary for either truth or warrant. Locked score: The precise 86 reflects excellent coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and charitable calibration, with a modestly lower evidential warrant marking the remaining step from possible accuracy to a full account of rational justification under determinism overall.

pro.words: Audience members raising their hands after a request display responsive action, but the performance must distinguish libertarian freedom from causally produced compliance.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The demonstration supplies an immediate and understandable instance of people responding to a request, making the intended intuition of voluntary action vivid and accessible. Principal limitation: The same outward response could arise from determined processing, so the example does not discriminate between libertarian freedom, compatibilist agency, habit, or programmed behavior. Live burden: The affirmative must identify an observable feature of the hand raising that entails genuine alternative possibility rather than ordinary causal responsiveness. Locked score: The precise 56 follows from acceptable clarity and some relevance, overwhelmed by very weak coherence, evidential warrant, and calibration because the performance illustrates behavior without establishing the metaphysical property it was introduced to demonstrate, leaving the central inference largely unsupported here.

con.words: A programmed computer could mimic the requested stimulus-response performance without free will, so raising a hand cannot alone demonstrate the libertarian freedom claimed.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The computer comparison supplies a decisive counterexample to the demonstration’s form, showing that responsive performance alone does not entail freedom because nonfree systems can mimic it. Principal limitation: The analogy defeats the evidential sufficiency of outward behavior but does not establish that human agents actually operate like programmed computers or lack libertarian agency. Live burden: The affirmative must provide a discriminator unavailable to the computer case, while the negative need only preserve the counterexample against this particular demonstration. Locked score: The precise 89 reflects exceptional coherence, evidence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration, with the bounded limitation concerning the broader metaphysics rather than its extraordinarily precise success against the specific hand-raising inference presented here.

con.words: Causal regularity enables rational interaction within a changing universe, while an ability to violate causality would allegedly undermine dependable reasoning rather than secure it.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move reverses the affirmative’s concern by presenting causality as a precondition for dependable inference and interaction rather than an obstacle to rational thought. Principal limitation: The compressed formulation does not distinguish causal explanation from strict determinism or establish why libertarian agency must violate causality instead of constituting a distinctive cause. Live burden: The negative must clarify how causal processes ground reason responsiveness, while the affirmative must explain nonphysical origination without making choices arbitrary. Locked score: The precise 72 reflects solid coherence, responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, moderated by weaker evidence and calibration because the reversal is suggestive but underdeveloped and does not fully answer the stronger challenge concerning epistemic trust in determined cognition.

pro.words: The seven arguments should be displaced by identifying their failures, while scientific method cannot exhaust relevant truth, leaving the negative a detailed rebuttal burden.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move appropriately asks critics to engage the announced arguments rather than dismissing the conclusion solely because it is metaphysical, and it preserves reasoning beyond laboratory procedure. Principal limitation: Presenting seven arguments does not shift the ultimate existence burden, and criticizing an overly narrow method does not establish that any particular argument successfully demonstrates a soul. Live burden: The affirmative must defend each inference and articulate a reliable nonempirical standard, while the negative must answer the strongest positive grounds rather than demand measurement alone. Locked score: The precise 67 reflects reasonable coherence, relevance, and clarity but weaker evidence, responsiveness, and calibration because the burden allocation overstates what the cumulative presentation has already earned decisively.

con.words: Mind may be a phenomenon produced by the brain, and reductionism need not deny conscious awareness, preserving consciousness while rejecting a separate soul.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply distinguishes explaining consciousness through brain production from denying conscious awareness, preventing the affirmative from treating physical reduction as elimination of experience. Principal limitation: Asserting production does not provide the mechanism or fully answer the qualitative and intentional properties emphasized by the affirmative, so the positive account remains limited. Live burden: The negative must explain how organized brains produce the relevant mental features, while the affirmative must show that incomplete production theory entails nonphysical substance. Locked score: The precise 76 reflects solid coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and generous calibration, tempered by moderate evidence because the reply successfully preserves a conceptual physical alternative without developing enough detail to establish that alternative as the actual explanation.

pro.words: Pain’s felt quality is directly known and exceeds merely observing or labeling a brain state, challenging reduction of experience to third-person description.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move sharply distinguishes first-person felt pain from an external neural description, preserving the qualitative datum that any satisfactory account must explain rather than eliminate. Principal limitation: A difference between access modes or descriptions does not establish that the experience and brain state are different substances, and the inference remains unstated beyond irreducibility. Live burden: The affirmative must move from epistemic difference to ontological difference and then show why a soul, specifically, grounds the felt quality. Locked score: The precise 67 reflects useful evidence contact, relevance, and responsiveness, offset by weaker coherence, precision, and calibration because direct acquaintance establishes the phenomenon more securely than the proposed nonphysical conclusion or entity explanation here presented conclusively.

con.words: Independent experiences, information, and interactions support treating split-brain hemispheres as distinct individuals, challenging the bare assertion that divided neural organization cannot yield distinct people.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move specifies independent experience, information, and interaction as criteria for individuating subjects, giving the split-brain evidence a structured connection to the number of apparent persons. Principal limitation: Functional independence may be incomplete, and the criteria are asserted rather than defended as sufficient for metaphysical personhood within the supplied exchange. Live burden: The negative must justify the individuation standard, while the affirmative must explain why one soul yields separately accessible knowledge and interaction patterns. Locked score: The precise 82 reflects strong coherence, evidence, responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, moderated by lower calibration because identifying two individuals remains a philosophically stronger claim than establishing divided processing or partially independent experiential centers alone.

pro.words: A soul allegedly grounds latent capacities, continuing identity, freedom, and unified experience even when particular functions are unexpressed through the body, like linguistic ability during sleep.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move unifies several affirmative themes by treating the soul as the bearer of both actual and latent capacities, thereby addressing impairment without surrendering personal continuity. Principal limitation: Packaging capacities within one proposed entity does not independently show that the package exists or explain why one soul rather than several bearers grounds the listed properties. Live burden: The affirmative must individuate the soul and derive consequences from latent capacities that differ from dispositions grounded in a physical person. Locked score: The precise 67 reflects reasonable coherence, relevance, and clarity, but weaker evidence, responsiveness, and calibration because the proposal organizes the affirmative account more effectively than it verifies the entity or resolves the package objection decisively here overall distinctly.

con.words: The affirmative has not shown why identity, freedom, unity, and latent capacities belong to one soul rather than several independent entities or descriptions.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move exposes an individuation burden often hidden by the soul label, asking why several attributed capacities constitute one entity rather than a convenient conceptual package. Principal limitation: A unified subject might itself provide a principled bearer, so the objection must engage the affirmative’s unity argument rather than treating aggregation as entirely arbitrary. Live burden: The affirmative must specify identity conditions tying the capacities together, while the negative must show that existing unity evidence cannot perform that work. Locked score: The precise 83 reflects excellent responsiveness, strong coherence, relevance, clarity, and charitable calibration, moderated by lower evidential warrant because the challenge reveals missing support but does not independently prove that no unified bearer exists beyond the label proposed.

con.words: Observed qualities can be collected beneath a soul label without demonstrating a transcendent entity, so classification alone cannot satisfy the existence burden.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move clearly distinguishes observed qualities from the existence of a transcendent bearer, directly attacking the inference from a useful package label to a real soul entity. Principal limitation: The criticism must allow that explanatory unification can support unobserved entities when independently constrained, so labeling is not automatically evidentially empty in every context. Live burden: The affirmative must derive constraints, predictions, or identity conditions from the soul beyond collecting capacities, while the negative must assess any offered unification fairly. Locked score: The precise 87 follows from outstanding coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and strong evidence discipline, with only a bounded limitation concerning whether the cumulative affirmative case supplies more structure than the label criticism acknowledges.

sections.title: Interaction, Brain Injury, and Survival Evidence

pro.words: The soul inference addresses phenomena matter allegedly cannot produce rather than temporary ignorance, so its force depends on demonstrating genuine physical impossibility.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move distinguishes an argument from alleged metaphysical impossibility from an appeal to temporary scientific ignorance, clarifying the intended structure of the affirmative’s case. Principal limitation: Stating that matter cannot produce the phenomena does not demonstrate impossibility, and the excerpt does not supply the missing argument against every physical or emergent organization. Live burden: The affirmative must establish principled impossibility rather than current explanatory absence, while the negative must engage those principles rather than merely predict future science. Locked score: The precise 75 reflects strong responsiveness, relevance, and clarity with decent coherence, moderated by weaker evidence and calibration because the conceptual distinction is useful but its application depends entirely on still-disputed impossibility claims.

con.words: Dillahunty invokes methodological naturalism without asserting philosophical naturalism, denying that prior commitment controls his rejection of the soul because he says evidence convinced him.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly answers the accusation of prior philosophical commitment by distinguishing a working evidential method from a universal assertion that only nature exists. Principal limitation: Personal intellectual history and disavowal of philosophical naturalism do not by themselves validate the chosen method or show that it accommodates every legitimate metaphysical inference. Live burden: The negative must defend methodological standards independently, while the affirmative must show those standards exclude relevant evidence rather than simply failing to confirm the soul. Locked score: The precise 81 reflects strong coherence, responsiveness, clarity, and exceptionally charitable calibration, moderated by lower evidence and burden relevance because rebutting motive and commitment does not fully settle the methodological dispute itself conclusively.

pro.words: Soul-body interaction is proposed as ontologically basic, needing no intermediate mechanism because further links create infinite regress, though interaction itself still requires confirmation.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move correctly notes that an explanatory chain need not continue indefinitely and offers basic interaction as a coherent stopping point rather than inventing an unsupported intermediate mechanism. Principal limitation: Calling interaction basic does not demonstrate that it occurs, specify its regularities, or answer how the proposed soul’s influence can be distinguished from ordinary brain causation. Live burden: The affirmative must provide evidence and constraints for basic interaction, while the negative need not demand a deeper mechanism before asking whether the asserted relation exists. Locked score: The precise 67 reflects respectable coherence and clarity but weak evidence, responsiveness, relevance, and calibration because the ontological classification answers one kind of how-question while leaving the existence and verification questions substantially untouched.

con.words: Ordinary bodily discomfort needs no soul explanation because a brain, nerve endings, and gravity suffice, while the asserted soul-body connection remains unconfirmed and lacks independent evidential support.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply separates an ordinary bodily experience from the soul hypothesis and directly notes that labeling interaction basic supplies no confirmation that attachment or influence occurs. Principal limitation: Explaining the cited discomfort through brain, nerves, and bodily conditions does not address every proposed mental property or establish that no soul participates in experience. Live burden: The affirmative must confirm interaction independently of examples already explained physically, while the negative must avoid treating one sufficient bodily account as universal disproof. Locked score: The precise 80 reflects strong coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration, moderated by moderate evidential warrant because the reply effectively defeats the cited example without resolving the complete interaction question across the debate.

pro.words: Brain injury may alter expressed personality and ability by damaging the soul’s physical instrument rather than changing or destroying the underlying subject.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly accommodates injury-linked changes by distinguishing the soul’s underlying capacities from their bodily expression, preserving logical compatibility between dualism and brain dependence. Principal limitation: Compatibility is not explanatory superiority, and the instrument account supplies no independent indication that an intact soul persists behind the altered personality or ability. Live burden: The affirmative must identify observations favoring disrupted expression over changed mentality, while explaining why specific injuries yield specific deficits under the instrument model. Locked score: The precise 74 reflects strong responsiveness, relevance, precision, and coherent burden contact, balanced against weaker evidential warrant and moderate calibration because the analogy answers a consistency objection but does not convert that consistency into affirmative survival evidence.

con.words: If brain damage prevents soul direction while the brain continues producing behavior, the soul contributes nothing necessary to explaining that behavior or its source.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply turns the instrument model against explanatory necessity: if behavior continues while soul control is blocked, the brain appears sufficient for the very work attributed to the soul. Principal limitation: Continued behavior may differ from intact agency or experience, so the inference requires care about which functions persist and which were supposedly contributed by the soul. Live burden: The affirmative must specify indispensable soul effects despite neural production, while the negative must compare impaired and unimpaired functions rather than treating all behavior alike. Locked score: The precise 81 reflects strong coherence, responsiveness, relevance, and clarity, moderated by evidence and calibration because the redundancy challenge is powerful but depends on functional equivalence that the excerpt does not fully establish universally.

pro.words: A determined brain allegedly cannot ground trust in its judgments, while metaphysical reasoning may establish impossibilities without experiment, challenging the negative’s epistemic standard.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move connects determinism to epistemic trust and reminds the audience that some impossibility claims may be evaluated through reasoning rather than direct experimentation. Principal limitation: It does not show why causally produced judgments cannot track evidence, and it combines that unresolved challenge with a broad methodological claim instead of answering the immediate survival evidence. Live burden: The affirmative must establish that alternative possibility is required for reliability and apply metaphysical reasoning specifically to physical impossibility. Locked score: The precise 56 reflects limited relevance and acceptable clarity but weak coherence, evidence, responsiveness, and calibration because neither component completes its inference and the combined reply does little to advance the immediate interaction or survival dispute conclusively.

con.words: Near-death experiences are not death, conflict with related claims, and permit hidden-target testing rather than serving automatically as evidence for survival or souls.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move distinguishes near-death from death, notes inconsistency among related survival claims, and proposes hidden targets as a discriminating method for information unavailable through ordinary perception. Principal limitation: The excerpt does not report completed results, and inconsistency among broader claims does not determine the evidential value of every individual experience. Live burden: Proponents must show verified inaccessible information and connect it specifically to a soul, while skeptics must evaluate actual tests rather than dismiss anecdotes categorically. Locked score: The precise 80 reflects strong coherence, relevance, clarity, responsiveness, and calibration, moderated by evidential warrant because the move supplies an excellent testing framework and cautionary comparison but not the decisive test outcome itself here presented.

pro.words: The seven metaphysical arguments allegedly remain undefeated, correlations are not explanations, and soul belief remains justified unless the negative supplies substantive defeaters.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The closing integrates the affirmative themes around grounding, correlation, and nonempirical truth, maintaining direct contact with the motion and presenting the case as cumulative. Principal limitation: It characterizes much of the negative response as mere possibility while underengaging verification, emergence, split-brain individuation, and the distinction between compatibility and necessity. Live burden: The affirmative must show that the seven arguments establish one soul rather than several explanatory gaps and demonstrate why physical accounts are impossible. Locked score: The precise 68 reflects solid relevance and clarity but only moderate coherence, evidence, responsiveness, and calibration because the synthesis is recognizable yet overstates how fully its crucial premises survived the detailed objections raised during the exchange overall.

con.words: The soul remains an undemonstrated label because physical impossibility and material interaction were not shown, leaving the affirmative’s central existence burden unmet.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The closing consolidates the central objections into a precise burden: demonstrate the entity, show physical accounts are barred, and identify the interaction rather than labeling mysteries. Principal limitation: The synthesis emphasizes unmet demonstration more than it explains consciousness positively, so its victory depends on the affirmative retaining the existence burden rather than physicalism being established. Live burden: The affirmative must provide independent entity verification and necessity, while the negative must remain open to nonempirical reasoning that yields genuinely discriminating consequences. Locked score: The precise 87 reflects exceptional coherence, responsiveness, relevance, clarity, and calibration with strong evidential discipline, moderated only because the conclusion supports withholding belief rather than proving the stronger proposition that no soul exists.

strengths: The opening distinguishes correlations from identity by comparing mental and neural properties, directly establishing the central nonphysicality route with strong responsiveness and clear burden contact.
The unified-subject argument connects one visual field to one experiencer, explaining why aggregated processing may not exhaust conscious unity or identify its bearer.
The brain-instrument replies engage injury evidence directly, explaining impaired expression through damaged access rather than denying observed dependence of personality and ability.
The closing integrates intentionality, unity, persistence, and agency into one metaphysical case, maintaining clear relevance to whether a soul grounds disconnected personal capacities.

blunders.text: The irreducibility argument assumes components lacking beliefs cannot collectively realize beliefs, but it does not establish why organization could never generate a novel system-level property.
The hand-raising demonstration shows responsive behavior but does not distinguish libertarian choice from caused performance, leaving its inference vulnerable to the computer comparison.
The instrument analogy remains compatible with brain damage but supplies no independent discriminator showing damaged access rather than altered mentality, limiting evidential force.

strengths: The necessity-versus-compatibility distinction redirects anecdotes and unexplained experience toward the affirmative burden, preventing a merely available soul interpretation from becoming automatic evidence of the soul's actual existence.
Split-brain and injury comparisons connect changes in knowledge, personality, memory, and behavior to neural organization, pressuring claims of one indivisible, unaffected personal subject.

The computer-response counterexample answers the hand-raising demonstration by showing that identical outward compliance can occur without the freedom the demonstration purportedly establishes, so the observed action alone remains inconclusive.
The closing consolidates verification, entity individuation, detectable interaction, and physical alternatives into a direct, specific demonstration burden that answers the affirmative synthesis.

blunders.text: The emergence reply preserves a physical alternative but offers limited positive support for emergence itself, so it blocks necessity more effectively than it explains experience.
The changing-label account is practical and responsive, yet it leaves underdeveloped why continuity judgments remain warranted across substantial physical and psychological alteration.
The claim that causality supports rationality is compressed and does not fully distinguish causal responsiveness from the stronger epistemic reliability challenged by the affirmative.

finalArgument.thesis: A soul best grounds unified consciousness, intentional thought, enduring identity, and genuine agency because these features resist identification with changing physical components alone.
premises: Mental properties differ from neural descriptions, so correlation alone leaves an explanatory bridge between physical activity and subjective, intentional consciousness that requires grounding.
Unified experience belongs to one apparent subject, while aggregate physical description names many processors and must explain why their organization produces a single experiencer.
Personal identity appears to continue through bodily and psychological alteration, making a persisting nonphysical subject a candidate ground for continuity and latent capacities.

Deliberation presents reasons influencing action, and the soul hypothesis interprets this top-down agency as activity originating from one unified personal subject who weighs reasons and directs action.
Brain dependence can remain compatible with a soul if neural structures operate as instruments that enable, constrain, or disrupt the subject’s expression and access.
finalArgument.conclusion: Together, these considerations support a soul as a unified and enduring subject explaining mental properties, continuity, and agency more comprehensively than correlation alone.

newArguments.title: Comparative integration test
newArguments.text: The affirmative considerations can reinforce one another rather than operate as isolated proofs. Subjective quality identifies what needs grounding, intentionality specifies mental direction, unity identifies the bearer, and persistence identifies continuity through change. A soul gains force only if one subject explains all four without merely renaming them. This approach strengthens the case by making explanatory integration the comparative standard while preserving the debate’s central metaphysical commitments and acknowledging that compatibility alone remains insufficient.

newArguments.title: Boundary and discrimination test
newArguments.text: The instrument account can distinguish damage to expression from destruction of the subject. If a soul remains while neural access fails, the account should specify which capacities are latent, which depend on functioning pathways, and what would count against impairment. Such conditions turn compatibility into a risk-bearing explanation. This adds no survival evidence, but clarifies whether brain dependence uniquely favors identity or remains consistent with constrained nonphysical agency, making the comparison more disciplined and informative.

finalArgument.thesis: No soul has been demonstrated because mental phenomena remain compatible with physical accounts, while brain dependence and unresolved verification burdens defeat claims of explanatory necessity.
premises: Compatibility with a soul does not demonstrate necessity, especially when organized brain processes can describe the same observations without positing an additional entity.

Split-brain organization and brain injury alter knowledge, personality, memory, and agency, closely connecting attributed personal functions with physical neural organization rather than separating them from it.
Calling unexplained capacities a soul supplies only a package label unless an independent method identifies the entity, distinguishes alternatives, and confirms causal contribution.
An immaterial cause changing material behavior should produce investigable manifestations, even when the proposed cause itself is not directly accessible through ordinary measurement.
Agency and accurate belief need not require libertarian freedom because caused cognitive processes can still respond to evidence, track reality, and distinguish external coercion.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, withholding belief remains warranted until a method demonstrates the soul, its necessity, and its interaction beyond what brain-based alternatives can explain.

newArguments.title: Comparative integration test
newArguments.text: A soul can be assessed by removing it from each explanation and asking what observed prediction or explanatory relation is lost. If brain organization already tracks memory, personality, divided awareness, and behavioral control, adding an inaccessible subject may change nothing. The soul becomes significant only when it generates a discriminating expectation unavailable to physical alternatives. This test reinforces the verification burden by converting general demands for evidence into a concrete comparison of explanatory contribution.

newArguments.title: Boundary and discrimination test
newArguments.text: The package objection can be sharpened by asking what determines the number and boundaries of souls. If unified function grounds one soul, divided function pressures that count. If biological continuity grounds one soul, altered personality requires explaining why it is secondary. A criterion must classify ordinary unity, split organization, impairment, and latent capacity consistently without adjustment merely to preserve the hypothesis. Entity verification therefore requires individuation, not simply attaching one name to collected capacities.

con.quote: We need something more than assertions.
